## Pull request overview

This pull request comprehensively addresses five interrelated filter parameter protocol issues across the ObjectStack codebase: inconsistent naming (`filter`/`filters`/`$filter`), naive AST detection, incorrect response field mapping, GET-by-ID parameter pollution, and lack of shared AST validation.

**Changes:**
- Introduced `isFilterAST()` structural validator and `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` constant in `@objectstack/spec/data` to replace naive `Array.isArray` checks with recursive AST validation
- Unified filter parameter naming: canonical `filter` (singular) for HTTP, `filters` (plural) accepted for backward compatibility, with normalization in protocol layer
- Fixed dispatcher response field mapping from incorrect `result.data`/`result.count` to spec-correct `result.records`/`result.total`
- Implemented GET-by-ID parameter allowlisting (only `select`/`expand` permitted) to prevent query parameter pollution
- Added `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema` documenting canonical HTTP query parameter names with coercion support

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 9 out of 9 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts | Added `isFilterAST()` recursive validator and `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` Set for structural AST validation beyond naive array checks |
| packages/spec/src/data/filter.test.ts | Added 19 comprehensive tests covering `isFilterAST()` validation: comparison nodes, logical nodes, legacy arrays, invalid arrays, recursive validation |
| packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts | Added `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema` with canonical `filter` param (deprecated `filters` for compat); updated `GetDataRequestSchema` to explicitly allow only `select`/`expand`; corrected FindDataRequest example to use structured QuerySchema format |
| packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts | Added 50+ tests for `GetDataRequestSchema` select/expand validation and `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema` coercion/naming |
| packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts | Fixed GET-by-ID to allowlist only `select`/`expand` params; corrected `handleApiEndpoint` response mapping to use `result.records`/`result.total` |
| packages/objectql/src/protocol.ts | Added `filters` → `filter` normalization; replaced `Array.isArray(options.filter)` with `isFilterAST()` for AST detection |
| packages/client/src/index.ts | Added canonical `QueryOptions.filter` field (deprecated `filters`); delegated AST detection to spec's `isFilterAST()`; sends `filter` (singular) HTTP param |
| content/docs/guides/api-reference.mdx | Updated parameter table to canonical unprefixed names (`filter`, `select`, `sort`); documented GET-by-ID allowlisted params; added OData endpoint note |
| ROADMAP.md | Documented completion of 4 protocol hardening items: filter parameter naming, `isFilterAST()` validation, GET-by-ID allowlisting, dispatcher field mapping |
</details>

The condition `this.isFilterAST(filterValue) || Array.isArray(filterValue)` has a logical issue. Since `isFilterAST()` already returns `false` for invalid arrays (like `[1, 2, 3]`), the fallback `|| Array.isArray(filterValue)` will cause ANY array (even non-filter arrays) to be JSON-serialized and sent to the server.

This means invalid filter arrays like `[1, 2, 3]` will pass client-side validation and be sent to the server, where they will either fail validation or be misinterpreted.

Consider either:
1. Remove the `|| Array.isArray(filterValue)` fallback so only valid AST arrays are serialized
2. Add a comment explaining why invalid arrays should be passed to the server for validation

The current implementation defeats the purpose of the new `isFilterAST()` structural validation.
```suggestion
             if (this.isFilterAST(filterValue)) {
                 // Valid filter AST → serialize as JSON in `filter` param
```
